records.supported_name_scope: The long downstream portion of fragment 14083 and fragments 14084–14085 follow Río Maipo. The names of fragment 14081, fragment 14082 and the initial cross-slope connection of fragment 14083 remain null. The official prose identifies Laguna Nacimiento as the river's source setting, but this does not demonstrate that the selected dogleg passes through that lake.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The supported corridor runs northwest down the upper Maipo past its separate mountain tributaries, north through the Las Melosas and San Gabriel surroundings, then past San Alfonso and San José de Maipo to the El Manzano bend. It turns west past Puente Alto and Pirque, southwest beside the Buin/Valdivia de Paine setting and north around the Isla de Maipo bend before continuing west through the Talagante–El Monte–Melipilla corridor. The lower route continues through the Chocalán, Huechún Bajo and La Floresta settings, then north beside the Santo Domingo area to the coastal mouth south of San Antonio. At its southeastern end, however, the selected line runs south, reverses north along the western Maipo volcano slope and then cuts west to the mapped receiving valley. Original IGN topography depicts the principal Maipo channel farther southwest, and does not establish that dogleg as a connected river or lake passage.
records.region: Central Chile, Metropolitan and Valparaíso regions, from the western Volcán Maipo headward setting through the Cajón del Maipo and central valley to the San Antonio–Santo Domingo coast.
records.candidate_name_role: Supported receiving-river identity for the long central and lower selected corridor; not a demonstrated name or continuous water route for the anomalous southeastern headward fragments.
records.completion_scope: The long named receiving corridor, central and western fragment transitions, tributary exclusions and coastal ending have been read against acquired primary maps. The southeastern 14081–14082 sequence and the initial straight western connector of 14083 have been inspected against original 1:100,000 topography, but a continuous actual water route matching them has not been established. They have not been replaced by the clearer Maipo channel. This is not a completed full-feature correspondence finding.
records.material_pending_reason: Primary topography does not establish the exact 14081–14082 northward dogleg and the initial straight westward 14083 connection as a continuous actual river/lake route. The main Maipo identity and downstream corridor cannot close this headward correspondence gap.

naming_scope_details.initial_headward_component: Unresolved short selected route on the western Volcán Maipo/Paso Maipú headward setting.
naming_scope_details.regional_source_lake_context: Laguna Nacimiento is identified in the original MMA webpage and sanctuary nomination prose as the Maipo source setting. Its inclusion in the retained headward dogleg is not established.
naming_scope_details.supported_main_river_component: Río Maipo from the receiving-valley setting west of the anomalous headward connector, through the Cajón del Maipo, central valley and lower coastal course.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Río Maipo coastal estuary/mouth near Llolleo, between San Antonio and Santo Domingo.
excluded_inferences: Do not apply Río Maipo uniformly to the two initial fragments and the unproven straight headward connector.
Do not replace the retained headward route with the clearer principal Maipo valley.
Laguna Nacimiento's documented regional source role does not establish a selected lake passage, a glacier identity or an exact official source point.

Alvarado, Argüelles, Cruz de Piedra, Barroso, Blanco, Negro, Volcán, Yeso, Colorado, Clarillo, Angostura, Mapocho and Puangue remain distinct tributary names; their complete upstream courses are not selected.
Embalse El Yeso and Laguna Negra are separate neighboring waters, not components crossed by the supported selected main corridor.
No Korean name, alternative Indigenous hydronym, legal naming date or exact contemporary channel/bank alignment is established.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 279.351 km value is the retained five-fragment modeled length, not an official Maipo river measurement. The two initial fragments and initial 14083 connector are not merely accepted as a normal generalized bend: their correspondence to actual connected water remains materially unproved. No point-by-point geometry revalidation or geometry correction was performed.

records.supported_name_scope: Dewar Lakes is supported for the separately mapped central lake group. Hantzsch River is supported at the lower receiving junction and final coastal continuation to Hantzsch Bay. The initial and long middle/southern tributary components have no established river name.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The northeastern start descends southwest, turns west around a broad northern elbow and then south through the long interior valley and Dewar Lakes. Below the lakes it continues south and southwest through a separate lake-rich tributary corridor, meeting the east-approaching Hantzsch River only near its Hantzsch Bay outlet. This is not the full named Hantzsch main river from the eastern interior; the named receiving identity cannot be propagated up the entire selection.
records.region: Central Baffin Island, Nunavut, Canada, from the northern interior stream-and-lake country through Dewar Lakes to Hantzsch Bay.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-river identity only; the long northern unnamed stream–lake route and Dewar Lakes are separate components.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded headward, branch-choice, lake-passage, tributary-junction and coastal-terminal correspondence for the complete single selected fragment. Four acquired original federal raster views give whole-route context and overlapping northern, middle and southern enlargements. Original source pixels and necessary separate local orientation overlays were read across the complete route. This supports the connected waterway corridor and lake sequence, not exact banks, every minor channel thread, or every component name. No unsupported inter-valley transfer was found.

naming_scope_details.lower_river_component: Short lower Hantzsch River below the northern tributary connection.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Hantzsch River opening into Hantzsch Bay.
excluded_inferences: Do not apply Hantzsch River uniformly to the northern approach, Dewar Lakes or the long southern tributary corridor.
The separately mapped McBeth River setting and upper east-approaching Hantzsch River are not selected upstream.

No separate name is established for the minor lakes, short interlake/outlet passages or northern and southern tributary reaches. No Indigenous alternative, formal naming date or Korean name is established.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 279.343 km value describes the retained single-fragment modeled stream–lake–river selection, not an official Hantzsch River length. Stepped paths simplify local bends, lake traverses, receiving junctions and the final coastal connection. The connected corridor is supported without exact-channel or point-by-point geometry revalidation.

records.supported_name_scope: Original INEGI topographic pixels support the local Los Saltillos approach to San Juan del Tuzal and the subsequent Arroyo de San Juan corridor to Laguna la Salinera. Beyond the lake, the selected model crosses extensive plains, settlements, roads and scattered intermittent drainage without one continuously mapped named river. Whole-route, receiving-river and unknown connector names remain null.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected northwestern start is near Coyotillos, west of Charcas. It approaches San Juan del Tuzal from the northeast, then follows Arroyo de San Juan south past Noria del Tajo and El Cedazo, east of Laguna Cornejo. It passes El Toro and enters Laguna la Salinera. The modeled continuation crosses the Cruces and Los Tajos surroundings, turns toward Santa Teresa and Moctezuma, passes the La Matanza–Estación Moctezuma corridor and Pozos de Matanza, and continues across the plain through San Felipe, San Francisco de la Dicha and the El Pozo surroundings. It passes north of Villa de Arista, near Saltillos and El Charquito, crosses the San Lorenzo–San Isidro highway corridor and bends north near Palos Altos. Its eastern arm passes Charco Blanco, Núñez, La Campana and the Pozos de Santa Ana surroundings, then crosses toward the El Coyote–San Juan Sin Agua plain. It continues past Santa Teresa and ends near San Martín, east of Palo Blanco and northeast of San Francisco. This is not an established connection to the distant Río Moctezuma or a verified named Río Salado.
records.region: Interior San Luis Potosí, Mexico: the Charcas–Laguna la Salinera corridor and the Moctezuma, Villa de Arista, Charco Blanco and San Martín plains.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded geographic and name-scope review of the entire actual selected route using the original INEGI Matehuala F1401 and San Luis Potosí F1404 topographic sheets. Overlapping readable original crops cover both northern ends and the full western, middle, southern-bend and eastern passages. Separate private orientation overlays were compared with unmarked source pixels. No selected interval lacks readable primary-map coverage. The unresolved issue is whole-route natural-channel and naming scope, not missing source material.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Complete readable primary cartography locates the full selected route and supports the northwestern named-arroyo and lake components. It does not establish one continuous named natural river across the long post-lake and eastern plain extensions. This is a feature/name-scope hold; whole-route and unknown connector names remain null.

naming_scope_details.supported_headward_stream_component: Arroyo los Saltillos, limited to the mapped local approach toward San Juan del Tuzal.
naming_scope_details.named_lake_setting: Laguna la Salinera; intermittent water body, not a river-name alias.
excluded_inferences: Do not extend Arroyo de San Juan or Arroyo los Saltillos over the complete modeled route.
Do not replace the unknown whole-route identity with Laguna la Salinera, an administrative basin or aquifer name.
The settlement Moctezuma does not establish correspondence with the distant Río Moctezuma; a regional Salado association does not establish a Río Salado hydronym.
Do not promote crossed or nearby tributary labels such as Arroyo el Tule, Arroyo los Tajos or other short plain streams to the whole selected line.
Absence of a continuously drawn channel is not proof of permanent dryness or absence of all episodic flood connections.
No exact name-transition vertex, surveyed source or mouth, complete surface-flow continuity, Indigenous alias or Korean name is established.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 277.622 km value is the retained inventory modeled-mainstem length, not an official length of any named arroyo. Its generalized route includes lake/plain crossings and connectors. Embedded map bounds and local projection were used only to orient private reading overlays; no source geometry was uploaded, edited, revalidated or matched by a new point-by-point acceptance test.

records.supported_name_scope: The source supports Caribou River along the upper, central and lower river corridor. Clearly selected named lake settings include McCaskill, Chawanski, the northern Manders arm, western/southern Commonwealth, Pollon, Baroni, Round Sand, Petrie, Caribou and Long lakes. Minor feeders and connector names remain null; only the selected portions of complex lake groups are identified.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The northwestern start goes southeast through the McCaskill–Chawanski lake approach, uses the northern Manders connection into Commonwealth Lake and leaves southward on Caribou River. The river proceeds southeast through the upper lake chain, turns south, then southeast/east into Caribou Lake. From the eastern lake arm it turns northeast, makes the broad lower northern elbow and descends through Long Lake before continuing east to the Hudson Bay opening southwest of Hubbart Point. Nearby tributary lakes and the northern coastal river system are not substituted for the selected route.
records.region: Northern Manitoba, Canada, south of the Nunavut boundary, from the northwestern lake country through Caribou River to the Hudson Bay coast by Hubbart Point.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-river identity and supported main river corridor below Commonwealth Lake, with distinct named lake components.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded correspondence for the complete single selected fragment using four original federal map exports: whole-route context and overlapping western, middle and eastern detail. Original pixels and separate private orientation material were inspected for the initial lake branch, Commonwealth outlet, upper lake chain, central Caribou corridor, Caribou Lake turn, lower bend, Long Lake and coastal ending. The connected river/lake corridor is supported. The generalized model cuts local bends and parts of lake shores and does not establish exact bank alignment or a channel thread around every island.

naming_scope_details.middle_lake_component: Caribou Lake, selected western-to-eastern crossing and northern outlet.
naming_scope_details.desilets_scope: Desilets Lake surroundings beside the selected southeastern lake-outlet corridor; no full separate-lake traversal asserted.
naming_scope_details.gagnon_scope: Western Gagnon Lake/Caribou River surroundings; no full eastern-lake-basin traversal asserted.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Caribou River opening onto Hudson Bay southwest/south of Hubbart Point.
excluded_inferences: Do not apply Caribou River uniformly to all the separately named lakes, the initial feeder or short unnamed interlake passages.
The northern Manders passage does not imply a traversal of the larger southern Manders basin; the western Commonwealth crossing does not imply its full northern basin is selected.
William Wright, de Rzonca, Fetherstonhaugh and the many adjacent middle/lower lakes are not automatically part of the selected mainstem.
The 277.556 km modeled route is not an official Caribou River length. No legal naming date, Indigenous alternative or Korean name is established.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Stepped display paths generalize narrow lake connections, islands, rapids and bends, lake crossings and the coastal outlet. Readable primary cartography establishes the connected selected corridor and named components, not every exact channel thread. No geometry modification or point-by-point revalidation was performed.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
